# Ps008 — Inch-valued coordinates labeled as millimetres

## Sources
- deduced from SI_UNIT(.MILLI.,.METRE.) semantics
- bug-report patterns "STEP file imported 25.4x too large", "model came in as 100 mm but was 100 inches", "wrong units mm vs inch", "unit declaration mismatched"

## Description

The SI_UNIT context declares LENGTH_MEASURE in mm. The CARTESIAN_POINTs and VECTORs encode coordinate values that the producer intended as inches (e.g., a "100mm cube" whose vertices are (0,0,0)..(100,100,100) but where 100 is actually the inch value, so the real-world dimension is 2540mm). The kernel cannot detect this — both unit declaration and coordinates are individually well-formed. Kernel accepts the file silently; tier-3 introspection (cross-checking PRODUCT.name conventions, schema header text, or dimensional plausibility against an expected size class) reveals the mismatch.

## Reproducer recipe

A 100x100x100 cube with SI_UNIT(.MILLI.,.METRE.) context. PRODUCT name and FILE_DESCRIPTION can hint at the producer's intent ("100mm cube") to make the mismatch detectable by metadata cross-check.

## Expected kernel behavior

A kernel cannot self-detect this in general, but it can expose the unit context and coordinate-extent envelope as metadata so that downstream tools (e.g., a DRC pass that knows the part's expected size class) can flag the mismatch. Some kernels offer a "smell test" mode that flags AABB extents outside a configured plausibility range.

## Notes

Tier-3 metric: AABB-extent-vs-expected-size cross-check; any metadata field naming a unit (PRODUCT.description, FILE_NAME author field) compared against SI_UNIT prefix.
